To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in one and two space dimensions the integrated density of the spectrum of a magnetic Schrödigner operator with Gaussian random potential is locally Lipschz continuous and that the low-energy spectrum is almost surely purely discrete for a Poissonian potential with finite-range repulsive impurities.
the integrated density is almost surely locally Lipschitz in the Gaussian case and almost surely pure point in the Poisson case.
the integrated density is Lipschitz continuous in the Gaussian case, whereas the density is only Hölder continuous.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical analysis of electronic properties of disordered solids.
the rigorous mathematical analysis of electronic properties of amorphus or disordered solids, which are often described by one-particle random Schrodinger operators.
the spectral properties of random Schrödigner operators, in particular with the existence of the integrated density, the Lifshits tail and the Anderson localization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the presence of a sufficiently strong random potential and a sufficiently weak magnetic field, Anderson localization takes place for all energies in all space dimensions.
the low-energy spectral subspace is almost surely localized for a large class of random potentials, whereas the high-energy spectral subspace exhibits extended states.

for all physically relevant cases of one- and two-dimensional amorphous solids with a random potential that is not too strong, the low-energy spectrum is almost surely purely discrete, the eigenstates are localized and the corresponding wave packets remain localized for all times.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integrated density-of-states approach is a very powerful tool to study the electronic properties of disordered solids.

the spectral properties of one-particle Schrödigner operators for amorphous solids are well understood in the high-energy regime and in one dimension for a Poissonian model with repulsive impurity potentials of finite range.

the integrated density and the density of states of random Schrodinger operators in a magnetic field behave very much like in the case without magnetic field, whereas the spectral properties of the Hamiltonian are more sensitive to the magnetic field.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are many robust results on the integrated density of the states of random Schrodinger operators for amorphous solids which have been obtained by different methods, and that there are also some results on Anderson localization.

, although there is a lot of progress on the rigorous understanding of the spectral properties of random Schrödingers operators in one dimension, the situation in higher dimensions is much less satisfactory.
the rigorous results are rather robust with respect to the random potential and the magnetic field.
